function: Over-the-air aggregation of low-rank gradient factors for wireless federated learning: Jacobi-SCA low-rank gradient compression with MIMO over-the-air computation beamforming and error feedback (pp. 3-4).
system: Uplink MIMO block fading, K=10 devices (half selected per round) with Nt=8 antennas, server Nr=8, SNR 20 dB; no RIS; frequency band not given (pp. 2, 4).
method: ResNet18 classifier trained with federated learning (supervised); Ota-LC compresses each local gradient into low-rank factors with one warm-started Jacobi SCA step, error feedback and over-the-air computation (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Channels: i.i.d. CN(0,1) entries for each device and round, constant per iteration; learning data: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, i.i.d. and Dirichlet(0.9) non-i.i.d. splits (p. 4).
test_conditions: FL training over the simulated channel at SNR 20 dB; accuracy versus channel uses (r=20) and versus SNR (T=250, Ncu=4000); CIFAR-10/100, i.i.d. and non-i.i.d. (pp. 4-5).
baselines: SGD without compression; Ota-CS [10], Ota-RLC [16] (over-the-air); PowerSGD [14], Top-K [7], Rand-K [8] (digital), all with error feedback (p. 4).
metrics: Test accuracy versus total channel uses, channel uses per round and SNR; training loss; channel uses needed for 70% accuracy (pp. 4-5).
complexity: Local compression O(nmr) operations and uplink payload O(nr+mr) instead of O(nm); compared with O(nmr(m+n)) for Ota-CS and Ota-RLC, O(mn log(mn)) for Top-K (pp. 3-4).
openness: Code at https://github.com/MingzhaoGuo/Ota-LC (p. 4); CIFAR-10/100 are public learning datasets; channels simulated.
q1_support: p. 4: "are generated from i.i.d. CN (0, 1) for all k and t". Custom i.i.d. Rayleigh channels; no standardized model, public ray-tracing dataset or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 5: "We also compare Ota-LC with the benchmarks for different SNR under T = 250 and Ncu = 4000". Only SNR and channel-use sweeps; CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, i.i.d. and non-i.i.d. cases are separate trainings, none a transfer to unseen conditions.
q3_support: p. 4: "Our method is compared with SGD without compression, as well as with five existing gradient compression methods with error feedback for wireless federated learning" (earlier designs Ota-CS [10], Ota-RLC [16]; non-learned Top-K [7], Rand-K [8]); p. 5: "Fig. 3(b) shows that Ota-LC outperforms other algorithms even in low SNR regimes".
q4_support: p. 3: "the local updates (14) require an order O(nmr) of basic operation"; p. 4 compares this with O(nmr(m + n)) for Ota-CS and Ota-RLC, as an aggregation-side cost, not the model size.
q5_support: p. 4: "the code can be found at https://github.com/MingzhaoGuo/Ota-LC"
notes: A letter, eligible. Area 7: the problem is over-the-air aggregation of low-rank gradient factors over MIMO with beamforming (Eqs. 20-22); the learned element is the ResNet18 trained across devices, and the compression step itself is a classical Jacobi SCA algorithm. q3: the classical baselines are Top-K, Rand-K and uncompressed SGD, and the earlier aggregation designs are Ota-CS, Ota-RLC and PowerSGD; Fig. 2 shows accuracy against channel uses and Fig. 3 accuracy at fixed budget and SNR. Ota-LC without error feedback (Fig. 3) is an ablation and is not counted. Reviewer to confirm q3 for this federated setting.
